introduction: This Process Definition Document establishes the enterprise Hardware Asset Management (HAM) and Configuration Management (CM) operational standard for a UK Tier-1 Trading Bank undergoing a critical multi-site Data Centre Migration. In direct compliance with Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) Policy Statement PS21/3, PRA SS1/21, and SYSC 15.9, this framework enforces an immutable, auditable lifecycle for all physical compute, storage, appliance, and network hardware assets. It governs every phase from procurement and goods receipt through staging, migration deployment, production operations, change control, and secure decommission/disposal. Central to this standard is an automated 'No Ticket, No Touch' operational policy where physical or logical divergence between ServiceNow Discovery and the CMDB baseline instantly generates Sev-1/Sev-2 Unauthorized Change Incidents, backed by mandatory state-transition approval gates and bidirectional synchronization between ServiceNow alm_hardware and cmdb_ci_hardware tables to maintain an operational integrity threshold exceeding 99.5%.

system_requirements.name: ServiceNow ITOM Discovery & IRE Engine
system_requirements.details: ServiceNow Utah/Washington DC release with HAM Pro, ITOM Discovery, Service Mapping, and Identification & Reconciliation Engine (IRE). IRE rules configure hardware serial number, asset tag, and MAC address as mandatory unique identifiers with IRE reconciliation priority rules favoring automated discovery over manual input.

system_requirements.name: ServiceNow HAM Data Model & Asset-to-CI State Synchronization Module
system_requirements.details: Bidirectional synchronization engine between alm_hardware and cmdb_ci_hardware tables. Enforces mapped state progression: alm_hardware install_status (Ordered -> In Stock -> In Use -> In Maintenance -> Retired -> Disposed) synchronously locked to cmdb_ci_hardware install_status and operational_status. State transitions to 'In Use / Operational' are strictly locked pending CAB Change Approval and Technical Readiness Token clearance.

Automated background reconciliation script scheduled post-discovery that compares discovered infrastructure deltas against approved active Change Requests. Any discrepancy generates an immediate Sev-1 (Trading Critical) or Sev-2 (Supporting Infrastructure) Unauthorized Change Incident, automatically locks CI attributes, and alerts Information Security and CAB.

process_steps.description: Upon physical arrival at the data centre loading dock, the DC Logistics and ITAM teams inspect physical packaging for tamper evidence, scan vendor serial numbers, and affix tamper-evident banking enterprise asset barcodes and RFID tags. The asset record in alm_hardware is transitioned from 'Ordered' to 'In Stock' (6) with substatus 'Pending Inspection / In Staging'. The ServiceNow HAM mobile scanning application automatically matches scanned serial numbers against the pre-allocated PO stubs. Any discrepancy, damaged item, or unlogged serial number is automatically quarantined in a secure holding area, and an asset alert is routed to ITAM.

process_steps.description: Under the authority of an approved Data Centre Migration Change Request, data centre technicians unbox and rack-and-stack the hardware into designated cabinets according to the rack allocation layout. Structured power and network cabling are connected. Technicians configure baseboard management controllers (iLO/iDRAC) on the isolated provisioning network. Automated ServiceNow ITOM Discovery is initiated against the staging management subnet. The ServiceNow Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) identifies the hardware via serial number and MAC address, establishes the bidirectional link to the existing alm_hardware record, and instantiates the cmdb_ci_hardware CI record with install_status='In Stock / Staging' and operational_status='Non-Operational' (2).

process_steps.description: Prior to any operating system installation or production traffic enablement, ServiceNow Discovery performs an exhaustive deep-scan of the hardware CI. Discovered attributes (CPU cores, physical memory, storage disks, HBA WWNs, NIC MACs, rack unit position, PDU port feeds, and firmware versions) are validated against the approved engineering design using automated ServiceNow Health rules. The CI and Asset records are checked for bidirectional synchronization between alm_hardware and cmdb_ci_hardware. Data integrity, completeness, and correctness scores must exceed 99.5%. If any attribute diverges, the technical readiness gate automatically fails, preventing promotion and notifying the Lead Configuration Manager.

process_steps.description: Formal promotion of hardware CIs to live trading operations requires passing a mandatory ServiceNow operational approval gate. The Change Advisory Board (CAB) and designated Important Business Service (IBS) Service Owner review the Technical Readiness clearance, the data centre migration test results, and the rollback plan. Upon electronic CAB sign-off in ServiceNow, the automated workflow simultaneously promotes alm_hardware to install_status='In Use' (1) and substatus='Operational', and cmdb_ci_hardware to install_status='Installed' (1) and operational_status='Operational' (1). The CI is bound into the live trading service dependency mapping, establishing the official production configuration baseline under FCA PS21/3.

process_steps.description: During ongoing operational life in the target data centre, ServiceNow ITOM Discovery executes automated daily scans across all IP ranges and management fabrics. The 'No Ticket, No Touch' policy is continuously enforced by automated reconciliation scripts. If ServiceNow Discovery detects any divergence from the CMDB baseline (such as an unapproved CPU/RAM modification, blade insertion, switch port modification, or new unmapped IP/MAC address) without an active, approved Change Request in state 'Work in Progress', the system immediately: (1) Locks the CI record, (2) Auto-generates a Sev-1 (for Critical Economic Functions) or Sev-2 (for supporting tiers) Unauthorized Change Incident assigned to Infrastructure Engineering and Information Security, (3) Triggers automated network isolation if the device is unrecognized, and (4) Logs a compliance event for FCA PS21/3 reporting.

step_risks_and_controls.risk: Data exposure from improperly wiped storage drives or untracked disposal leading to catastrophic regulatory fines under GDPR and FCA rules.
step_risks_and_controls.control: Dual-custody sign-off, serialized tamper-evident transport containers, and mandatory ADISA Level 8 certificate validation attached directly to ServiceNow asset record before disposal closure.

success_criteria: 100% of retired hardware assets possess serialized ADISA-certified destruction documentation in ServiceNow within 5 days of removal.
process_steps.estimated_duration: 2 to 3 business days from de-rack to destruction certificate upload via SLA-backed on-site ITAD standby and parallel sanitization pipelines
process_steps.description: When hardware reaches end-of-life or is retired during data centre consolidation, an approved Decommissioning Change Request is initiated. Migration engineers physically unrack and power down the unit, transitioning alm_hardware to install_status='Retired' (7) and substatus='Pending Disposal / Sanitization', and cmdb_ci_hardware to install_status='Retired' (7) and operational_status='Non-Operational' (2). The asset is transferred to a secure, badge-controlled DC disposal cage. An ADISA-certified IT Asset Disposition (ITAD) vendor conducts on-site NIST 800-88 R1 / ADISA Level 8 cryptographic erasure or physical shredding of media. The serialized destruction certificate is uploaded into the ServiceNow alm_hardware record, updating install_status to 'Disposed' (8), updating cmdb_ci to 'Disposed' (8), and permanently deactivating discovery scanning for that serial number.

constraints: Strict regulatory oversight under FCA PS21/3 and PRA SS1/21 mandates uninterrupted operational resilience and zero unapproved drift on Critical Economic Functions (CEFs).
Physical access to data centre cages and halls is strictly restricted by automated biometric controls tied to approved ServiceNow change tasks.
Zero-tolerance policy on untracked configuration items; undocumented hardware discovered on the network must be isolated via automated network access control within 15 minutes.
Disposal processes must achieve ADISA-certified cryptographic data erasure or physical degaussing/shredding with auditable chains of custody.
assumptions: ServiceNow Utah/Washington DC release is deployed with HAM Pro and Discovery/Service Graph Connectors active.
Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) rules are calibrated with hardware serial number and asset tag as mandatory unique identifiers.
Network access controls and automated discovery schedules have been provisioned across all target data centre subnets.
ServiceNow ITOM Discovery patterns are fully configured for all physical compute, storage arrays, and network fabric switches.
All hardware suppliers provide electronic advance shipment notifications (ASNs) with serial numbers and MAC addresses prior to delivery.

critical_success_factors.description: Complete real-time traceability of Configuration Items supporting Important Business Services (IBS) to demonstrate operational resilience compliance under FCA PS21/3.

change_management.versioning_rules: All documentation and ServiceNow system configuration baseline updates follow semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Major updates require Head of ITAM and Head of Operational Resilience sign-off; minor updates require CAB Manager approval; patches reflect automated rule fine-tuning.
change_management.change_request_process: Modifications to baseline CM and HAM configuration policies, schema definitions, reconciliation rules, or operational thresholds must be submitted via ServiceNow Standard/Normal Change requests and require unanimous approval from the Configuration Control Board (CCB) and Lead Configuration Manager.

governance_requirements: Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) Policy Statement PS21/3 - Operational Resilience: Systems, configurations, and dependencies underpinning Important Business Services must be documented, auditable, and continuously maintained.

Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA) Supervisory Statement SS1/21 - Operational Resilience: Hardware dependencies for Core Trading Services must maintain rigorous configuration control and change governance.
FCA SYSC 15.9 - Operational Risk and Resilience Systems & Controls: Mandatory logging of configuration alterations, automated detection of rogue changes, and full asset audit trails.
ADISA Standard 8.0: Asset Disposal and Information Security Alliance compliance for secure hardware disposal, disk sanitization, and destruction certification.
purpose: Establish an authoritative, auditable, and automated Hardware Asset Management (HAM) and Configuration Management (CM) operational framework in ServiceNow for a UK Tier-1 Trading Bank. The process guarantees precise bidirectional state synchronization between alm_hardware and cmdb_ci, enforces 'No Ticket, No Touch' change governance, mandates strict operational approval gates, and maintains >99.5% CMDB integrity to satisfy FCA PS21/3 operational resilience mandates.
process_name: Enterprise Hardware Asset and Configuration Management Process
scope: Applies to all physical compute infrastructure (rack servers, blade chassis, hyperconverged nodes), network devices (core/leaf switches, routers, firewalls), storage hardware (SAN arrays, NAS filers, backup appliances), and hardware security modules (HSMs) deployed across all primary, secondary, and co-location data centre facilities supporting UK trading bank operations.
